pharmacology.text: Paroxetine is the most potent and one of the most specific selective serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5-HT) reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). It also binds to the allosteric site of the serotonin transporter, similarly to escitalopram, though less potently so.

uses.text: Paroxetine is primarily used to treat major depressive disorder, obsessive–compulsive disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, social anxiety disorder, and panic disorder. It is also occasionally used for agoraphobia, generalized anxiety disorder, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, and menopausal hot flashes.

sideEffects.text: Common side effects include drowsiness, dry mouth, loss of appetite, sweating, trouble sleeping, and sexual dysfunction. Serious side effects may include suicidal thoughts in those under the age of 25, serotonin syndrome, and mania.

summaryZh: 帕羅西汀是一種選擇性5-羥色胺再吸收抑制劑型的抗憂鬱藥，其藥物形態為鹽酸帕羅西汀，在臨床上常用於憂鬱症、強迫症、社交焦慮症、廣泛性焦慮、PTSD等疾病的治療。
summaryZhHans: 帕罗西汀是一种选择性5-羟色胺再吸收抑制剂型的抗抑郁药，其药物形态为盐酸帕罗西汀，在临床上常用于抑郁症、强迫症、社交焦虑障碍、广泛性焦虑、PTSD等疾病的治疗。

fact.en: Paroxetine was first described in 1974 and binds the serotonin transporter more tightly than any other SSRI. It is on the World Health Organization's list of essential medicines.
fact.zh: 帕羅西汀在 1974 年首次被描述，它與血清素轉運體的結合比任何其他 SSRI 都更緊密，並列於世界衛生組織的基本藥物清單中。
fact.zhHans: 帕罗西汀在 1974 年首次被描述，它与血清素转运体的结合比任何其他 SSRI 都更紧密，并列于世界卫生组织的基本药物清单中。
